recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a dead man's switch: nightly-sync pings a monitoring endpoint when it finishes, and an alert fires if no ping arrives by about 03:30, hosted either in a small self-hosted container on the Synology or on a hosted free tier; it also notes the token expiry should be fixed separately.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You said you want to know when nightly-sync dies, specifically because it crashed before the email step four nights running and nothing told you. Nobody asked for centralized logging as its own goal; that's a proposed means, not the stated need.
labels.Deleted: A full Docker log-aggregation stack (ELK/Loki/Grafana, "everything in Docker"). It doesn't solve your actual problem: you said you won't read logs, so a nicer place to not look at still leaves you blind.
labels.Bottleneck: Detection, not storage. The script already has a working success signal (the email); it has no failure signal. That's the gap to close.
labels.Checked myself: This is based only on what you've told me (one cron job on edna, email on success, no other alerting, Synology with Docker available). I haven't looked at the script, crontab, or NAS.

note: Classed LARGER because the reply offers a self-hosted Docker container on the Synology as an equal option, though it is only one alert either way.
